svg.title: The order of the instructions is the size of the image
svg.desc: Two stacks of Docker layers drawn to scale - a 3,140 MB naive stack whose pip-install layer alone is 1,455 MB, and a 466 MB ordered stack - joined by a fat amber arrow annotated with five changes and their individual savings from .dockerignore at minus 250 MB to using ONNX instead of torch at minus 851 MB, plus two rebuild timelines showing 214 seconds struck out against 11 seconds, and a crossed-out attempt to shrink an image by deleting files in a later layer.
svg.text: The order of the instructions is the size of the image
rebuild after a ONE-LINE code change
the COPY invalidates every layer above it
RUN rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists in a LATER layer
deleting in a later layer does not shrink
the image. The bytes are still in the
earlier layer. Delete in the SAME RUN.
...and where do these images actually run? -> Week 24
